newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina hikes VAT on bank loans back to 21 pct.
newsitem.headline: Argentina hikes VAT on bank loans back to 21 pct.

text.p: Argentine shopkeepers Tuesday protested the government's decision to double VAT on bank loans to 21 percent from 10.5 percent, reversing a measure brought in last April.

The measure announced in the December 2 issue of the government Official Bulletin will make personal loans more expensive. Banco Rio gave the example in Clarin newspaper of a two-year loan for 5,000 pesos paying 23 percent interest, which now rises to a real interest rate of 25.2 percent.

The Official Bulletin announcement says: "The current economic situation is ripe for introducing some limitations correcting some certain imbalances ... that were affecting competition in the market."
But the shopkeepers' lobby CAME said the measure will put the brakes on Argentina's tentative economic recovery.
"Consumer activity in recent years has been generated by credit and not by increased purchasing power of consumers," CAME said in a statement.
